problem: Existing visual semantic navigation methods extract scene priors from instant observations and store them in neural episodic memory or explicit scene representations, but forget and underuse these priors, causing repeated exploration, sparse effective knowledge, and wrong decisions.
motivation: Object-goal navigation in unseen scenes needs spatial patterns and object co-occurrence relations. Making full use of hierarchical priors (local map, global commonsense, retrieved context) and inferring unobserved regions should improve exploration efficiency and decision quality.
key_idea: HSPNav combines an egocentric semantic-map Local Scene Prior, a commonsense relational-graph Global Scene Prior, and attention-based retrieval between them, with a context-based semantic map completion network (CAE-SMCN) that augments the local prior, all trained with DRL.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that hierarchical priors, together with completion of unobserved map regions using context associations, improve prior and policy learning over existing methods on MP3D and HM3D.
method: Local Scene Priors (LSP): egocentric semantic map built from observations, encoding spatial layout and observed objects
Global Scene Priors (GSP): commonsense relational graph of object co-occurrence/spatial relations
Attention-based retrieval: retrieves contextual memories from the GSP closely related to the current LSP
CAE-SMCN: Semantic Map Completion Network with Context Association Exploitation module that infers unobserved regions on the egocentric map, yielding augmented LSP
DRL navigation policy: trained with deep reinforcement learning on the hierarchical priors; sim-to-real transferred

setting.backbone: DRL policy with semantic-map encoder, graph encoder, attention retrieval and CAE-SMCN (trained; details not in abstract)
setting.training_data: MP3D and HM3D scenes via DRL (details not in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric observations building a semantic map (exact modalities not stated in abstract)
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D and HM3D scenes; not stated explicitly)

results: The abstract claims HSPNav outperforms existing methods on MP3D and HM3D and generalizes to real-world settings via sim-to-real transfer. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and ablations are unknown
Relies on a commonsense graph and semantic mapping, whose quality may limit performance
